hypothesis: A large fraction of Request243's unresolved trades is an artifact of sparse minute next-open references. Replaying the already-chosen policy decisions against actually observed historical one-second aggregate opens, with a predeclared expiry and deadline, should materially reduce unresolved execution without changing the policy.
population: Request243 May11-20 locked calibration episodes only; policy is refit exactly from the same Apr30-May8 chronological training blocks.

execution_contract.source: Massive historical one-second aggregates, already verified available under current entitlement
execution_contract.decision_feature_use: none; second bars are execution labels only and are fetched after policy actions are frozen
execution_contract.entry_order: first observed positive one-second open at or after policy ENTER decision plus latency
execution_contract.exit_order: first observed positive one-second open at or after policy EXIT decision plus latency
execution_contract.missing_policy_exit: use Request243's precommitted hot_t + 29 minute liquidation deadline, never hindsight last row
execution_contract.missing_observed_open: unresolved, never cash and never a favorable later price

forbidden: using one-second future data as decision features
choosing a favorable fill within the expiry window
using a hindsight last observed row as liquidation
opening June or any new holdout because of this result
claiming synthetic one-second aggregate opens are actual broker fills
claiming profitability or promotion from this diagnostic
next_if_pass: Request245 should audit ENTER-now versus WAIT continuation values under the same frozen policy using reconstructed execution, strictly chronological out-of-sample blocks.
next_if_fail: Keep the action-value experiment frozen and repair execution observability or the order contract before another policy-learning experiment.
